purpose: Single source of truth for dashboard data assets. Read by scripts/validate-data.js (node scripts/validate-data.js). Paths are relative to the nfldashboard repo root. Only files inside this repo are validated; the producer's unversioned data/shared handoff is the sync script's input, and Edge keeps its own props-board copy via refresh-props-board.ts (out of scope).

assets.label: Props board (producer export)
assets.note: The versioned data/shared copy ships with the deploy; the root copy is the browser fallback and is kept in sync by sync-shared-data.sh. Edge's src/data copy is refreshed only via refresh-props-board.ts and is intentionally not validated here.

assets.label: Mike Clay projections (PDF extraction)
assets.note: Root file is the extractor's direct output and the canonical source; data/shared copy ships with the deploy. No embedded timestamp: the manifest's as_of comes from the original file's mtime at sync time, which Git does not preserve on checkout — so this repo verifies internal manifest consistency only. Exact source-vintage verification lives producer-side (fantasyfootball freshness-provenance test).

assets.label: Full-season schedule (weeks 1-18)
assets.note: Root file is the builder's direct output; deep invariants (team counts, week windows) are covered by test_schedule_data.py. No embedded timestamp (mtime provenance is not checkout-safe), so the dashboard validates internal manifest consistency only; exact vintage is verified producer-side.

assets.label: Roster snapshot (Supabase teams+players with Madden overlay)
assets.note: The browser loads rosters live from Supabase; this committed file is the versioned snapshot used as the ESPN-updater baseline, deploy artifact, and hermetic-test player fixture. No embedded timestamp (mtime provenance is not checkout-safe), so the dashboard validates internal manifest consistency only; exact vintage is verified producer-side.

assets.label: nflverse team-season efficiency (2012-2025)
assets.note: Canonical copy ships with the deploy; root copy is the browser fallback kept in sync by sync-shared-data.sh. Vintage comes from the research file outside this repo, so provenance is verified for internal consistency only (producer-side freshness test covers exact vintage sourcing).

assets.label: Freshness manifest
assets.note: Optional by design: an absent manifest means no freshness stamps, never blocks rendering. Every sources entry must map to an inventory freshness_key and vice versa.

assets.label: Draft capital (2027-2028)
assets.note: Optional: loadAllData() soft-fails to null when absent.

assets.label: EA Madden official ratings map
assets.note: Optional overlay used only by the Matchup Lab player ratings.

assets.note: Not deployed to the dashboard; freshness-tracked in the manifest only.

assets.label: Supabase table: nfl_teams (live runtime)
assets.failure_behavior: loadAllData() awaits nfl_teams alongside players and transactions; on any error the page replaces the body with a red error screen and logs to console — no view renders.
assets.fallback_policy: None in the browser. Team colors/abbrs feed the committed nfl_rosters_2026.json snapshot and the in-page ABBR_TO_TEAM map for line lookups; there is no live-team fallback.
assets.test_fixture: Deterministic data-feed tests intercept the Supabase REST endpoint and synthesize 32 team rows (id/name/abbr/division/primary_color, no cap fields) from the committed roster snapshot — see test-fixtures/README.md.
assets.note: Runtime dependency, not a repo file: inventory records its contract so the validator can enforce the documentation. The validator never contacts the network.

assets.label: Supabase table: nfl_players (live runtime)
assets.failure_behavior: loadAllData() awaits nfl_players (paginated at 1000 rows); on any error the page replaces the body with a red error screen and logs to console — no view renders.
assets.fallback_policy: None in the browser. The committed nfl_rosters_2026.json is a deploy snapshot of this table used as the ESPN-updater baseline and test fixture, not a live fallback.
assets.test_fixture: Deterministic data-feed tests intercept the Supabase REST endpoint and serve the committed nfl_rosters_2026.json rows (with team_id linkage added) — see test-fixtures/README.md.
assets.note: Runtime dependency, not a repo file; documented contract only.

assets.label: Supabase table: nfl_transactions (live runtime)
assets.failure_behavior: loadAllData() awaits nfl_transactions (ordered by sort_date desc); on any error the page replaces the body with a red error screen — same path as the other two tables.
assets.fallback_policy: None in the browser. Normalized ESPN rows reach this table only via the explicit update_rosters_from_espn.js --write path (idempotent tx_id; migration supabase/migrations/20260903_espn_transactions_tx_id.sql). Dry-run output is inspectable only and is not a live fallback.
assets.test_fixture: Deterministic data-feed tests intercept the Supabase REST endpoint and serve the static, clearly-labeled synthetic fixture test-fixtures/nfl_transactions.json — see test-fixtures/README.md.
assets.note: Runtime dependency, not a repo file; documented contract only. The Moves newswire, team gains/losses, and home stats all read this table.

assets.label: nflverse games.csv (live market lines)
assets.failure_behavior: loadGameLines() catches and records MARKET_LINES_ERR; game cards render without spread/total/moneyline badges (schedule tab shows an empty line slot) instead of erroring the page.
assets.fallback_policy: None: there is no committed market-line source. The committed schedule.json carries kickoffs/venues only. build_full_schedule.py is the offline builder for schedule shape, not for live odds.
assets.test_fixture: Deterministic data-feed tests intercept raw.githubusercontent.com/nflverse/** and synthesize a deterministic 2026 REG games.csv (lines derived per game) from the committed schedule.json — see test-fixtures/README.md.
assets.note: Fetched at runtime by the schedule tab and home marquee; graceful degradation on failure.
